name: Andaz London Liverpool Street
insider_take: A Victorian railway hotel reimagined as London's most vibrant boutique stay, where historic grandeur meets contemporary edge in the heart of the City.
whats_special: This stunning Grade II listed building was originally built in 1884 as the Great Eastern Hotel, serving as the grand gateway to Liverpool Street Station. The hotel seamlessly blends its ornate Victorian architecture with bold, modern design - from the original Masonic Temple converted into a striking event space to rooms featuring exposed brick walls and contemporary artwork. Its location puts you at the epicenter of London's financial district while being perfectly positioned between trendy Shoreditch and historic Spitalfields Market.
pro_tip: Book a Heritage Room to experience original Victorian features like soaring ceilings and period windows, while still enjoying modern luxury amenities. The hotel's five restaurants and bars each occupy beautifully restored spaces with their own unique character.
dont_miss: Step outside to explore the vibrant Sunday markets at Spitalfields (2-minute walk), discover cutting-edge galleries and vintage shops in Shoreditch, or take the short stroll to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. The hotel's central location also provides easy access to the City's historic churches, including the nearby St. Botolph's and a quick tube ride to St. Paul's Cathedral.
pros: Prime Liverpool Street location with direct access to train station and financial district
Contemporary design in beautifully converted Victorian railway hotel building
Complimentary minibar and local phone calls included
Hyatt Privé benefits including room upgrades and daily breakfast
cons: Busy transport hub location can be noisy
Premium pricing reflects central London location
